learning_outcomes: Explain when GraphRAG outperforms flat chunk retrieval and when it is overkill.
Implement a hierarchical retrieval pipeline (RAPTOR-style) and evaluate its impact on Recall@K.
Compare dense retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and late-interaction (ColBERT-style) using a small benchmark set.
Design a multi-representation index that separates search-friendly summaries from generation-ready full passages.
Run an ablation study to identify which retrieval upgrades actually improved grounded answers.

key_facts.fact: GraphRAG combines knowledge-graph construction with retrieval to answer multi-hop and global questions; verify current (2024-2025) open-source implementations and recommended pipelines before positioning it as default.
verification_notes: Confirm active GraphRAG repositories and their maintenance status.
Verify when graph traversal improves recall/faithfulness vs adding latency/complexity.

key_facts.fact: RAPTOR-style hierarchical retrieval uses recursive summarization and tree search to retrieve both coarse and fine-grained context; verify canonical papers and tooling support in 2025.
verification_notes: Confirm reproducible baselines and common failure modes (summary drift).
Verify recommended tree depth, chunk sizes, and summarization prompts.

key_facts.fact: ColBERTv2-style late-interaction retrieval (token-level MaxSim) can improve precision but increases storage and latency; verify 2024-2025 benchmarks and practical deployments before recommending it.
verification_notes: Validate trade-offs vs modern dense retrievers and cross-encoder rerankers.

categories.name: Hook
checks: Hook lands in the first 30 seconds (bold claim or provocative question).
Frames a real failure case where basic RAG fails.
Sets a mission and payoff for advanced retrieval architectures.

categories.name: Structure
checks: Clear progression: GraphRAG → RAPTOR → ColBERT → comparisons → decision matrix.
Key terms defined once and reused consistently.
Ends with a Holocron summary and actionable checklist.

categories.name: Labs
checks: Labs are missions with copy/paste prompts or code and expected outputs.
At least one lab is a retrieval ablation study.
At least one lab compares precision/recall across retrievers.

categories.name: Visuals
checks: Diagrams readable on mobile (no tiny text, no overlap).
Each advanced architecture has a dedicated diagram.

categories.name: Accuracy
checks: Time-sensitive claims verified or explicitly marked with sources.
No outdated model/product references in current recommendations.

categories.name: Engagement
checks: Uses tension (failure modes) and aha moments.
Includes at least 2 interactive moments or self-checks.
Avoids long blocks of unbroken exposition.

rules: Any category score below 8/10 fails the MASTERPIECE gate even if total >= 59.

must_be_true_facts.fact: Retrieval quality (recall/precision) constrains generation faithfulness; poor retrieval forces guessing.
RAPTOR proposes recursive clustering and summarization to retrieve both global and local context from long documents.

sources.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval

must_be_true_facts.fact: ColBERT uses late interaction (MaxSim) between query and passage token embeddings to improve retrieval precision.

sources.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT

dont_claim: Don't present GraphRAG as universally superior; it trades simplicity for multi-hop reasoning.
Don't claim RAPTOR or ColBERT are default recommendations without verifying 2025 tooling and benchmarks.
Don't use time-sensitive model names, context limits, or pricing without verification.
Don't imply retrieval upgrades automatically improve answer faithfulness without evaluation evidence.
